title: Matt Hardy - 'TNA-AEW Matches Shouldn't Have Happened In The First Place' - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Clark ,
50 minutes ago
During a recent appearance on “The Ariel Helwani Show,” Matt Hardy expressed his belief that this year’s WWE WrestleMania 42 pay-per-view event felt “very prostituted” due to the sheer number of ads. He said,
“It feels very mainstream. They have all the advertisements and everything else. It feels very different from standard WWE. I think it’s hard for a lot of people to kind of grasp that WWE changes. I can say this being older, I sometimes hate change. It is definitely so evolved and so different from what the initial concept of WrestleMania was as an event. It felt very prostituted because all the ads and everything else.”
READ MORE: AJ Francis Comes To The Defense Of Carlos Silva
READ MORE: TNA President Carlos Silva – ‘I Don’t Like Being Called A Little B**** On Social Media’
“If you have these big matches between big stars, these matches need to be good. They need to have time. They need to have a good payoff at that point, because that’s what you’re building to. I feel like the TV is the vehicle that you build these matches, and you tell stories, but once you get to these PPVs and WrestleMania, that’s where you have to deliver the goods. No doubt about it.”
During the same podcast, Hardy commented on the growing controversy surrounding canceled crossover matches between TNA Wrestling and AEW talent. He said,
“Well, in my honest opinion, I think if we are partners with WWE and WWE’s laid out how we’re working together with TNA, and AEW is its own entity, we probably… shouldn’t do AEW–TNA bookings”
“It probably should have never been set… from the beginning, and I think going forward that would be the case now.”
